# isRelative

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a relative path.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isRelative() — Checks whether a value is a relative path. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code></p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isRelative(path: string): path is string;
```

The exact complement of `isAbsolute`: anything that does not start at a root, which includes the empty string.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description               |
| :-------- | :------- | :------------------------ |
| `path`    | `string` | The string path to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a relative path; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `path` to `string` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isRelative("docs/readme.md"); // => true
isRelative("./a"); // => true
isRelative(""); // => true
isRelative("/var/log"); // => false
isRelative("https://example.com/a"); // => false
```
